Placement: XMASS sits in its own cavern in the Kamioka mine; no source read gives a coordinate for it, so the Atlas's Mozumi-mine (Super-Kamiokande) point is referenced. Hall position is not published in the papers read.
XMASS-1.5 (a larger successor) is named only as a plan in the project description; no design report naming it was read, so it is not recorded as an experiment.

physics_goals.quote: The XMASS project aims to detect dark matter, pp and $^{7}$Be solar neutrinos, and neutrinoless double beta decay using ultra pure liquid xenon. The first phase of the XMASS experiment searches for dark matter.
physics_goals.value: Detect dark matter, pp and 7Be solar neutrinos and neutrinoless double beta decay with ultra-pure liquid xenon; the first phase searches for dark matter

summary.plain: XMASS was a detector holding 832 kg of liquid xenon in the Kamioka mine in Japan, built to look for dark matter by watching for its faint flashes of light. It ran from 2013 to 2019, saw no dark matter, and set limits on several kinds of dark matter.
summary.technical: Single-phase liquid xenon scintillation detector: 642 PMTs viewing 835 kg of xenon in a copper vessel, inside a 72-PMT water-Cherenkov muon veto, at 2700 m.w.e. Stable data taking Nov 2013 - Feb 2019 (1590.9 live days); 97 kg fiducial volume. Full-dataset WIMP-nucleon limit 1.4e-44 cm^2 at 60 GeV/c^2; annual-modulation, Migdal and bremsstrahlung searches for lighter WIMPs.
